references.text: David acknowledges that God desires truth in the inner being, which stands in contrast to those who appear righteous outwardly but are full of hypocrisy and wickedness within.

The Lord criticizes the people for their hypocrisy, honoring Him with their lips while their hearts are far from Him, paralleling the appearance of righteousness outwardly while being full of hypocrisy and wickedness inwardly.

Jesus condemns the Pharisees for their hypocrisy, cleaning the outside of cups and dishes while their inside is full of greed and evil, resembling those who appear righteous outwardly but are full of hypocrisy and wickedness within.

Jesus points out the Pharisees' hypocrisy by being righteous in the eyes of people, yet God knows their hearts, reflecting the contrast between outward righteousness and inner hypocrisy and wickedness.
Peter warns against false teachers who will introduce destructive heresies and deny the Lord, pointing to hypocrisy and wickedness hidden behind a facade of righteousness.
